newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles Board opposes tax limitation measure.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles Board opposes tax limitation measure.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted on Tuesday to oppose a ballot initiative that would limit the ability of local governments to impose fees, assessments and taxes.
The Board voted 3-2 to oppose Proposition 218, which will appear on the November 5 ballot.
The proposition would require that a majority of local voters in an election approve any increase in general taxes. It would also limit local government's use of fees and assessments.

Los Angeles County Chief Administrative Officer David Janssen warned the supervisors last week that the proposition would substantially reduce local government revenues, eliminate assessments and fee exemptions for all levels of government and increase governmental operating costs.
He said the measure would effectively eliminate the library assessment and put the fire protection district assessment at risk.

"Proposition 218 threatens the reliability of any tax, assessment, fee, or charge based on revenue source, as the electorate is granted initiative authority to reduce or repeal any such tax, assessment, fee or charge," Janssen said.
In a separate development, proponents and opponents of Proposition 218 testified in Sacramento, Calif., before a joint state Senate panel about the impacts of the proposal.
